mathematical_content: Select a nonempty finite family of admissible coprime rational approximating pairs, with every denominator greater than one, first logarithmic height strictly above an arbitrary L, and each successor height strictly above (2/delta) times its predecessor. Delta is already any real, including zero and negative values. A new generic construction selects an infinite sequence of arbitrary objects from a cofinal real-height set, with arbitrary time-dependent threshold F; its finite and empty-without-start forms and the complete arithmetic recovery compile. A separately rechecked new reduced selector removes positive kappa and gives unconditional existence for irrational centers when kappa<=2. Fixed coefficient one, actual coprimality, natural denominators, strict bounds and the original finite interface are retained. Public generic selection versus local Roth packaging is a completed BORDERLINE design question, not a proof or user blocker.

module_context_overrides.Roth/Main.lean: Main separately chooses numerical parameters, reduced rational approximants, and balanced integer degrees before a polynomial contradiction.277 is the finite recursive approximant selection step. It consumes reduced-denominator cofinality, rather than proving it, and does not supply integer degree balancing or the final exponent theorem.
module_context_overrides.Roth/LeanEval.lean: LeanEval gives a quantified uniform approximation lower-bound interface.277 chooses finitely many intermediate witnesses with prescribed logarithmic gaps; it does not establish that uniform endpoint.

Roth.exists_reduced_approx.comparison: 274 produces one reduced admissible pair beyond each natural threshold, proving cofinality through finite fibers and Dirichlet where appropriate.277 consumes that selector to construct a whole finite family with strict logarithmic starting and successor bounds. The new all-kappa and subcritical proofs independently replay274 templates; these remain new mathematics, not existing mathlib facts.

Roth.approxSet.comparison: 267 defines the fixed-quality pair predicate.277 constructs a separated finite family of its members with coprimality and denominator bounds. Predicate definition and recursive witness existence are distinct.

Roth.approxSet_den_le_finite.comparison: 269 proves bounded-denominator slices finite.277 needs unbounded reduced admissible witnesses and transports their denominators to logarithmic cofinality, then recursively selects. Local finite slices alone do not provide reduced witnesses or arbitrary recursive growth.

Roth.reduction.comparison: 271 rescales the real center and integer numerators, preserving infinite pairs with exponent loss.277 keeps the center and exponent fixed and selects a finite sparse chain. Their maps, quantifiers and outputs differ.

Roth.exists_m.comparison: 275 chooses a sufficiently large natural dimension satisfying numerical square-root and quotient inequalities.277 consumes an arbitrary nonzero dimension as the number of rational witnesses and constructs their logarithmic spacing. It does not choose the dimension or prove those scalar inequalities.

Roth.exists_delta.comparison: 276 selects a small positive real delta preserving quantitative eta/gamma inequalities.277 accepts any real delta; its logarithmic gap is a multiplier constraint and need not mean increasing heights when delta<=0. It does not prove the continuity or eta/gamma bounds used to choose delta.

pair_action: Keep the distinct selector, approximation predicate, numerical parameter and finite-chain interfaces. Recommend the verified kappa weakening and generic cofinal-height separation for future implementation; retain the original production API during this review. Public generic sequence API scope remains a completed design assessment.
